items.title: Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration for Long-Horizon Tasks
items.summary_1line: LLM-based agents are increasingly used to complete complex, long-horizon tasks without human intervention. To make progress toward the task goal, agents need to perform different duties, such as planning and verificat...
items.editor_note: Targets long-horizon tasks by dynamically assigning duties like planning and verification.

items.title: EvoTeam: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Teams

items.title: MA-Mesh: Resilient Multi-Agent Collaboration via Role-based Self-Healing
items.summary_1line: Effective collaboration in multi-agent systems requires mechanisms for coordination and adaptability in dynamic and uncertain environments. However, existing multi-agent systems rarely model resilience explicitly, ins...
items.editor_note: Makes resilience explicit with role-based self-healing.

editorial.tldr: Late-October arXiv papers pushed LLM multi-agent collaboration away from fixed workflows, toward decentralized belief-conditioned actors, goal-aware role assignment, evolving teams and calibrated confidence. The thread so far is research-only, with no shipped framework behind it.
editorial.whats_new: Two Nov 4 papers shift focus to failure and measurement: MA-Mesh adds role-based self-healing, and TandemBench benchmarks how decision models split work between agents.
editorial.why_it_matters: Research is moving from 'how agents collaborate' to 'how teams recover and how to measure coordination', the questions that decide whether multi-agent setups hold up in production.
editorial.take_for_builders: Treat these as research signals: if you run multi-agent pipelines, test what happens when one role fails mid-task before adopting any of these methods.

status.detail: Academic papers only; resilience and benchmarking now join the earlier coordination-design work.

beats.headline: Goal-aware roles, evolving teams and calibrated confidence

open_questions: Does any open-source agent framework adopt role-based self-healing like MA-Mesh?
Do TandemBench results get reproduced on other multi-agent systems?
Do the dynamic-team methods report cost or latency overhead versus fixed workflows?
